hook: Chronic low-effort stimulation does not just distract you. It degrades the baseline you need to feel satisfied by anything else.
topic: Dopamine baseline erosion from constant phone use
body:
**Chronic low-effort stimulation does not just distract you. It degrades the baseline you need to feel satisfied by anything else.**

Here is the mechanism. Your dopamine system operates relative to a baseline. When you repeatedly flood it with easy, low-effort stimulation — a scroll, a swipe, a quick check — the system recalibrates. The baseline moves up. Higher inputs are now required to produce the same response.

This is why a book feels slow. A conversation feels boring. A walk without your phone feels like deprivation. It is not that those things became less interesting. It is that your reference point for stimulation moved, and they can no longer reach it.

The practical result: people who use their phone heavily report lower satisfaction from activities that used to feel rewarding — focused work, creative output, in-person conversation, physical activity. The phone did not crowd those things out on the calendar. It made them feel worse by comparison.

The recalibration goes the other direction too. Reduce the low-effort input for long enough and the baseline drops back down. Deep work starts to feel engaging again. Conversation starts to feel sufficient. The boredom you feel in the first week of a phone protocol is not permanent — it is withdrawal. It has a known timeline.

Expect 10 to 14 days before the baseline shifts. Work through it, not around it.

Full 30-day rebuild timeline in the link in bio.
